there is a great deal of history to contend with when talking about the mustang it appeal to a large segment of american driver is impressive and to some degree a mustang lover will not be swayed by better performance found in foreign automobile that s not the point their loyalty is to the mustang brand first and foremost with that history of loyalty ha also come a great tradition of performance tuning these car so that there are several appealing option available to someone who ha some money to spend and want a true high end performance machine they will all cost you though the ford produced cobra svt start at about 34 000 while both saleen and roush make impressive model that will cost 35 000 40 000 or more this review however concentrate on the model at the other end of the scale the entry level affordable mustang coupe the base mustang come in three option level standard deluxe and premium starting at about 18 000 and going up 500 or so with each level engine drivetrain the base mustang come with a 3 8 litre v6 which make 193 hp and 225 lb ft of torque it is a dramatic step down from the v8 available on the higher end model both in performance and aesthetic where the v8 ha the throaty growl you expect from a muscle car the v6 of course doe not married to 4 speed automatic it is relatively quick but not overly impressive especially in the low end you ll be able to merge into traffic and pas without discomfort but is that really the performance level you want if you re buying a mustang i think we re looking for a little more performance and to get it you need to step up to the v8 the transmission is another sore spot if you have to get the v6 stay with the default 5 speed manual instead of upgrading to the automatic you maximize the performance of the engine and still get some performance feel with the stick but the automatic is awful early shift still some lag when you mash the pedal not good the automatic increase your price by almost 800 so i wouldn t bother unless you have to for those who have grown up on today s front wheel drive vehicle it is also worth noting that this is a rear wheel drive car yes it come with traction control now but you will still be surprised if you get into rain or snow and try to gun the engine the rear end is twitchy and you ll have a hard time getting it back into shape once it go exterior the mustang retains it burly muscle car appearance the high rear end and sloping windshield into the fake hood air intake give it it distinctive appearance that ensure you won t be confused with any other car on the road that definitely ha some appeal in an era when you sometimes can t tell the jaguar x type from a taurus individuality is good with that said some of the old fit and finish concern remain the cover on the fake air dam are flimsy and look ready to come off at a moment s notice those air dam are another pet peeve it smack of pretend performance to include the hood intake with those behind each door they re not functional for my money you can leave them off next year the available on the premium model 16 inch machined aluminum wheel are a positive though they re beefy sporty and fit well with the mustang style interior remember that you re essentially buying a detuned sport car so the interior is not necessarily designed for touring you slip down into the bucket seat and while they re not impossible to get in and out of some may find the extra effort needed to accomplish this annoying when inside the seat are comfortable enough though if you re any taller than me 5 11 you may be a little cramped control are conveniently located and are standard ford issue the leather wrapped steering wheel available in the premium model is a nice extra touch while on the road a driver unfamiliar with the mustang may have a few complaint wind noise while reduced from earlier model year is still more noticeable than it should be part of the price you pay for that distinctive appearance in addition be aware that visibility is not on par with a larger higher ride sedan again part of the price you pay for getting into a sport car where you sit low the rear seat are utile but not overly comfortable child will have no problem sitting there but larger adult will be somewhat cramped especially on longer ride miscellaneous ford includes some decent option remote keyless entry 6 way power driver s seat and an in dash 6 cd changer are standard in the premium model the ab and traction control are also nice and offset a bit the difficulty driver may experience with the rear wheel drive conclusion ford market the mustang to a very specific market of american driver who appreciate the history the muscle car feel and aren t looking for a cookie cutter accord or camry to drive around for about 20 grand you get a decent ride a distinctive appearance and reasonable power the trade offs are iffy quality some slightly old technology in the engine transmission and design and poor visibility if you re comfortable with that trade this is the car for you if true performance is your goal with the mustang consider stepping up to the higher end model available from either ford or one of the performance tuning outfit like saleen or roush
